findings.text: Power management helpers expose acquire and release of a runtime reference for the device associated with an interrupt domain, with lookup of that device from domain state returning absent when no domain is present.

Handler configuration interface allows replacing the flow handler for an interrupt number, installing a chained handler together with handler data, and installing chip plus handler plus name in sequence.

Status configuration and CPU notification interface allows modifying descriptor status flags with trigger propagation and notifying every active descriptor chip about online and offline CPUs when supported.

Hierarchical chip helpers forward common operations to the parent data element, covering acknowledge, mask, mask plus acknowledge, unmask, end of interrupt, shutdown, enable, disable, startup, affinity, type, vcpu affinity, wake, resources, state access and pre redirect.
Chip state and vcpu affinity query interface resolves the descriptor for an interrupt number and walks toward parents until a chip advertises the requested capability, then invokes it.

Migration, affinity restore, message composition and sparse lock interface exposes per interrupt migration away from a departing CPU, restore on incoming CPU, MSI message composition by nearest capable ancestor, and exclusive sparse table locking.
Proc visibility is valid only when the descriptor is not hidden and not chained and has at least one action; otherwise validity is cleared. An alternate build provides an empty updater.
Chained identity holds exactly when the descriptor action pointer equals the distinguished chained action object and is non null.
Dedicated setters only add their respective no request, no thread and no probe markers without clearing other accessor state.
Combined clear and set of settings is confined by a modify mask, so bits outside that mask are preserved on both operations.
Status modification refreshes derived data flags for no balancing, per CPU and level from settings and adopts the settings trigger mask when it is not none, then refreshes proc validity.
Parent chain traversal for hierarchy depends on build configuration: one variant follows the parent link, the other always ends the walk.
Resource acquisition and release at descriptor level and at parent level are optional: absence of the corresponding chip callback is treated as success or no action.
Migration is skipped when the chip or its affinity setter is absent, and also when the interrupt is per CPU or not started or its effective affinity does not include the current CPU.
Pending affinity moves are cleared when the pending mask no longer intersects online CPUs; otherwise a pending move may be reused for migration and optionally cleared by the caller.

Online restore applies only to managed affinity interrupts that have an action and a chip and whose affinity includes the incoming CPU; single target interrupts are left alone unless housekeeping isolation requests a move.

Handler installation, chained data installation, status modification, chip state access and vcpu affinity resolution all execute under a scoped descriptor acquisition combined with either bus synchronization or descriptor locking.
CPU online and offline dispatch and both fast end of interrupt flows hold the per descriptor raw spinlock while reading the chip pointer and invoking chip callbacks and event handling.

Offline migration holds the per descriptor lock while migrating one interrupt and scheduling affinity notification work; online affinity restore iterates under sparse table exclusion plus per descriptor interrupt safe guard.

Descriptor state observed includes a lock, status accessor flags, internal state flags, depth, the embedded interrupt data, action pointer, handler data, pending mask, affinity notification hook, and redirect target CPU.

Interrupt data state observed includes owning domain with power device, parent link, chip pointer, interrupt number, trigger and balancing markers, and affinity masks including effective and pending forms.

Chip interface observed is a table of optional callbacks for lifecycle, masking, acknowledge, end of interrupt, affinity, type, vcpu affinity, wake, resources, state access, CPU hotplug, redirect, message composition and forced move completion, plus flags controlling hotplug and wake behavior.

Acknowledge oriented fast end of interrupt flow checks power and action eligibility under lock, accounts the event, masks one shot lines, acknowledges hardware, runs handlers, then conditionally unmasks and signals completion.
Mask oriented fast end of interrupt flow masks and acknowledges first under lock, then on eligibility accounts and runs handlers before conditionally unmasking and signaling completion.

Parent lifecycle helpers degrade gracefully: shutdown falls back to disable, startup falls back to enable, disable falls back to mask, enable falls back to unmask, affinity type and vcpu operations report unsupported when the parent lacks them, and wake skip is treated as success.

Offline migration completes any pending move, masks chips that cannot move in process context, reuses a usable pending mask, shuts down managed interrupts with no online target, otherwise retries with all online CPUs after resource exhaustion, and unmasks before reporting whether affinity was broken.
Fast end of interrupt handlers serve as flow entry points invoked with a descriptor pointer and internally synchronize, account, mask, acknowledge, dispatch events and complete the interrupt.
CPU hotplug entries iterate all active interrupts to dispatch per chip online and offline callbacks, migrate everything off the departing CPU, and restore managed affinities on the incoming CPU.
Several parent forwarding helpers dereference the parent link and parent chip without an absent check, so callers must guarantee hierarchy depth and initialization or risk invalid access.

Migration can break configured affinity by falling back to all online CPUs, shut down managed interrupts with no online target, and warn when effective affinity contains only offline CPUs, so affinity expectations do not survive CPU removal.
Redirect affinity handling reports a dedicated done status after recording the first CPU of the destination set and updating effective affinity.

Lookup failures use distinct negative results for unsupported operation when no ancestor implements the callback, invalid identifier when no descriptor is found, and missing device when a chip pointer is absent during traversal.

Status vocabulary observed includes hidden, no request, no thread, no probe, no balancing, per CPU, level, proc valid, trigger sense and modify masks, plus internal one shot and affinity pending and managed shutdown markers.
